name: Sara Gupta

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel. We are independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What is a normal shift on the grocery-delivery support line like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the team that gets orders after the easy apology has failed. A customer says the cold food arrived warm, and I compare the packing scan, driver time and what actually reached their doorstep. My two-year college diploma gave me the record side; years on calls taught me to ask one more question. I sometimes use AI to tidy a reply, but I check the facts and make the correction myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you and your household count on from this work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Diego, my partner, cooks at a neighbourhood café, and we pay rent on a small flat. Our two daughters are grown and cover their own costs. I am a team lead but still earn about the ordinary agent wage; we have five months of expenses saved. A rota cut would be a rent problem, not just a job-title problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team a tidier apology note is fine, but the spoiled food still has to be replaced. If AI remains a small helper, we can keep checking the scans ourselves. Nobody is asking a computer to smell a warm carton through a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our paid queue should remain, and Diego's café should carry on. Five months saved covers a short mishap without asking our daughters for money. I use AI sometimes for wording already, but I don't mistake a polished message for a correct refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I'll keep leading the paid delivery-complaints queue and verify the packing scan before approving a replacement. If the plateau carries on into its first year, I'll use the same occasional draft help and check it against the order record. We will keep paying rent from wages rather than drawing down savings for ordinary bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. The job stays recognisable and both wages still arrive. A customer can be calm at the end of a call even when the delivery is still late. I prefer to solve the order, not just soothe the voice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What catches a wrong replacement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The scan may show the bag left the store, but the photo can show the wrong doorway. I ask which items were actually warm before approving a whole order. That's ordinary checking, not a new skill invented by the AI draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your daughters for help with a bill?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The five-month reserve is ours to use for an actual gap, and the daughters have their own bills. Diego and I can adjust a small expense before putting a rent worry on them.

say: I'd keep **packing scans** checked before approving replacements.
I'd say a polished **apology note** is not the same as a corrected order.
think: I expect my **paid queue** and Diego's café wage to continue.
I know occasional **AI wording** does not make refund decisions for me.
do: Keep leading **paid delivery complaints** and check scans before approving replacements.
Use existing **AI draft help** occasionally, verifying every reply against the order record.
feel: **Calm** about wages, while still focused on correcting the actual delivery.
S0.quote: A customer can be calm at the end of a call even when the delivery is still late.
fieldNote: She has **two-year college training** and strong complaint skill but earns typical agent pay despite leading the team.
Her occasional **AI wording** is existing practice; this scenario adds no new AI learning action.
Five months saved protects a gap, while **rent and both wages** remain ordinary household facts.

steps.text: Keep paid delivery-complaint queue and check scans before approving replacements

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the agents the machine can answer a missing-item chat quickly, but it must not close a warm-food complaint without a remedy. I would bring a group request to the union for paid correction shifts and a record of wrong auto-closures. A bot can close a ticket and leave a broken grocery bag on somebody's doorstep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some of my team hours could go if simple chats vanish. I have used AI for wording now and then, but I haven't learned the new closure-audit dashboard that checks which complaints a bot marked solved. I would try that after seeing it catch a real error, not from a sales slide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll join colleagues in the union request for paid human correction authority and published shift changes. If a paid real-case demonstration catches a spoiled order the bot called solved, I'll learn the new AI closure-audit dashboard by comparing a week's closures with packing scans and customer photos on paid time. I'll keep handling paid escalations while the team rota remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about paid hours, but curious about one useful check. I don't need the machine to like me; I need a customer to get the replacement they were owed. A group record can show whether the tool actually works.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the paid correction worker need to do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Reopen the order, approve a refund or replacement and tell the customer what changed. A worker who can only read the bot's answer is not a correction worker. The union request should name that authority in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you trust the new dashboard?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare a week's bot closures with the packing scans and customer photos, on paid time. If it finds the warm food the bot called solved, I can learn the tool. If it merely produces a nicer chart, I won't make my team depend on it.

say: I'd seek **paid human correction** with power to refund or replace an order.
I'd ask the union for **published shift changes** and wrong-closure records.
think: I fear **team hours** could shrink as simple chats disappear.
I would learn the **new AI dashboard** only after paid evidence shows it catches a real error.
do: Join a **union group request** for paid correction authority and published shift changes.
Learn **AI dashboard** if paid real-case demo catches error; compare bot closures with packing scans and customer photos on paid time.
Keep **paid escalation calls** while the team rota remains.
feel: **Anxious** about fewer paid hours, with some control through a tested tool and group request.
S1.quote: A bot can close a ticket and leave a broken grocery bag on somebody's doorstep.
fieldNote: Her **union request** seeks paid reversal authority and public rota changes, not a presentation alone.
She commits to **new AI learning** only if a paid real-case demonstration shows the audit dashboard catches mistakes.
Her existing **AI wording habit** does not itself count as learning a new tool.

steps.text: Join union group request for paid refund/replacement authority and published shift changes
Learn AI dashboard if paid demo catches error; compare closures with packing scans/photos on paid time
Keep handling paid escalations while the team rota remains

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Diego full thinking AI by 2028 could take our whole delivery-support queue before the 2031 robots reach packing or kitchens. I would ask with my colleagues for a written cut timetable and a paid human route for spoiled food complaints. Somebody must still make a refund real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My lead role might end with the queue. Five months saved is a pause button, not rent for the rest of our lives. Diego's café wage is useful, but it would not cover the flat and food alone for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I'll join the staff group's written demand for closure dates and paid customer correction, and keep leading paid calls while there is a rota. If the support queue ends in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for a posted paid produce-inspection shift at the local warehouse only after checking its written weekly hours and after-travel wage with Diego against our rent and essentials. I'll start that job only with a signed paid offer and safe lifting instruction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I can handle an angry call, but I cannot manufacture a paid week in a warehouse. I would not spend five months' reserve on a course whose job has not been posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why inspect produce?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know how food arrives damaged, but I have not worked a warehouse floor. I would need the employer to show me safe lifting before taking the paid duty. Robots about 2031 could reach parts of that work, so I would treat it as a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the warehouse does not post a shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would look at other posted local paid jobs and our written rent budget, not count a waiting list as income. If the contact-centre calls still pay, I keep them until they actually end. Our daughters are not a wage plan.

say: I'd join a **staff group demand** for cut dates and paid customer correction.
I'd tell Diego **2028 AGI** reaches complaints before 2031 warehouse robots.
think: I think the **lead queue** could end in the first year.
I know **five months saved** and Diego's café wage cannot cover rent indefinitely.
do: Join the **staff group demand** for written closure dates and paid correction while keeping paid calls.
After queue closure, apply for **posted paid produce inspection** only if written weekly hours and after-travel household pay cover rent/essentials.
Start **warehouse duties** only after a signed paid offer and safe lifting instruction; otherwise search other posted paid jobs against rent budget.
feel: **Alarmed** by possible loss of the whole paid queue and limited savings.
S2.quote: Five months saved is a pause button, not rent for the rest of our lives.
fieldNote: Her **staff-group demand** is for written closure dates and paid authority to correct spoiled-food errors.
The warehouse application follows **queue closure** and checks written weekly hours plus after-travel household rent coverage.
Signed paid acceptance and **safe lifting instruction** precede duties; posted local jobs are fallback if warehouse shifts are absent.

steps.text: Join staff group demand for written closure dates and paid customer correction
Keep leading paid support calls until queue closure
Apply after closure for posted paid produce work if written weekly hours/after-travel household pay cover rent/essentials
Start duties after signed offer and safe instruction; otherwise search posted paid jobs against rent budget

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years allows us to show the employer which bot closures are wrong and demand a paid human correction rota before 2031. I would use an audit dashboard if it proves useful, but I wouldn't call a new screen permanent safety. Warehouse robots arrive around 2034, later than the thinking work on our phones.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build a record of spoiled-order errors while keeping my team-lead wage. That might qualify me for a paid quality-review job, though full AGI could review records too. I need an actual posted role, not a certificate and a hope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep the paid lead rota and ask with union colleagues for posted paid review shifts with authority to refund customers. If one is posted, I'll take a paid trial on real disputes and complete required quality training only if the employer covers fees and paid study hours. In the first year after 2031, if my lead hours are cut, I'll apply for a still-posted paid review role only if its written weekly hours and after-travel wage with Diego's actual pay cover rent and essentials; I'll leave the lead shift only after a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years lets me learn what the review role really does. A review job is only useful if somebody can correct the order and draw a wage for it. The machine may reach the review work too, and I want that risk said aloud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the posted review role has no power to refund?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I wouldn't take a title that can only repeat the machine's decision. The union request is for correction authority and paid hours, and I would ask to see both on the vacancy notice. A course alone would not fill the rent gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no paid review shift appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep any paid lead shifts that remain and search other posted local paid jobs against our rent budget. I would not pay for training without a posted destination or treat five months saved as a salary. I would also keep sharing the wrong-closure record with the union.

say: I'd seek **paid review shifts** with refund authority and a real vacancy.
I'd say **2034 robots** are later than AGI's effect on screen work.
think: I can build **error evidence** while lead wages continue.
I know a **review title** cannot guarantee safety after full AGI.
do: Keep **paid lead shifts**; join union request for paid refund authority; if no posted review role, search paid jobs against rent budget.
Take **paid trial** only for posted review work with refund authority; complete required training only with employer-funded fees and paid study hours.
After 2031 cuts, apply for **posted paid review** with refund power if written after-travel weekly household pay/hours cover rent/essentials; sign before leaving.
feel: **Anxious** despite preparation because review work could also face AGI.
S3.quote: A review job is only useful if somebody can correct the order and draw a wage for it.
fieldNote: She treats a **paid trial** and real refund authority as tests of the review role, not a title alone.
Any required **quality training** needs employer-funded fees and paid study hours for a posted paid opening.
Application follows **actual lead-hour cuts** and written household rent coverage; she keeps paid shifts until a signed offer.

steps.text: Keep paid lead shifts until signed offer; without review post, search paid jobs against rent budget
Join union request for posted paid review rota with refund authority
Trial posted paid review; after 2031 lead-hour cuts apply if written after-travel household pay/hours cover rent/essentials
Complete required quality course only for posted paid role with employer-funded fees and paid study hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our daughters a decade is time to look at real rent and wages, not a promise that somebody will pay us to stop working. By 2036 I will be sixty-eight. If the support queue still exists, I may still want a paid shift, though full AGI could end it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five months saved today does not settle ten years of rent. Diego's café work and mine may change, and I will not assume a pension payment I have not seen. I might prefer a smaller flat over a frantic job move if paid calls end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting in 2026 Diego and I will compare our actual rent, savings and wages each year and keep paid review or support shifts while offered. We'll look at smaller accessible flats nearby, including bus fares to both workplaces, but move only if a real lease cuts our total monthly housing and travel bill. In the first year after 2036, if AGI ends paid calls and the budget still needs wages, I'll seek posted paid local work rather than assume rent savings alone replace my pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but the long warning lets us measure a smaller flat before making a move. A cheaper headline rent can disappear in bus fares. I want the numbers and a real door key before I tell our daughters we are settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a smaller flat worthwhile?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A signed lease we can afford, a safe entrance as we get older and a lower combined monthly rent and bus bill. A smaller flat would help us only if the combined rent and bus bill really falls. I would not move for an advert alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your daughters to support the move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. They have their own rents and may want to visit, but I don't want their wages in our plan. Diego and I can show them the new address once the lease is real. We should make the sums work ourselves.

say: I'd compare **rent and travel** before moving to a smaller flat.
I'd say **2036 AGI** could end calls even if I still need a wage.
think: I cannot assume a **pension payment** or help from our grown daughters.
I would move only for **lower total monthly costs**, not a cheap rent advert.
do: Review **rent, savings and wages** with Diego yearly while keeping offered paid shifts.
Move to a **smaller accessible flat** only with a real lease and lower total rent-plus-bus costs.
After 2036 call closure, seek **posted paid local work** if household still needs wages.
feel: **Anxious** about future rent and income, with time to check a real move.
S4.quote: A smaller flat would help us only if the combined rent and bus bill really falls.
fieldNote: She does not invent **pension entitlement** or adult-child support to close the future rent gap.
The **move is conditional** on an affordable signed lease and a lower total monthly housing-and-travel bill.
Even with cheaper housing, she seeks **posted paid work** after 2036 call loss if wages remain necessary.

steps.text: Review rent savings and wages yearly while keeping offered paid shifts
Move to smaller accessible flat only with signed affordable lease and lower total rent-plus-bus costs
Seek posted paid local work after 2036 call closure if household still needs wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because a team lead's skill could stop earning before our rent does. Written closure dates, paid human correction and a real job notice with weekly pay and hours would help. I want the right to put a mistake right, not a nicer way to apologise for it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the customer actually received the replacement, not only whether a ticket was closed. The food on a doorstep is the real result. I would like workers and customers to be able to correct the record together.

headlineQuote: I want the right to put a mistake right, not a nicer way to apologise for it.
portrait: At **fifty-eight**, Sara leads grocery-delivery complaints with a two-year diploma and strong case judgment.
She earns **typical agent pay** despite her lead role, with five months saved, rent and a partner on café wages.
She uses AI **occasionally for wording**, then tests a new closure-audit dashboard on paid real cases when slower change arrives.
Fast AGI threatens her **whole queue**; longer horizons shift her attention to paid review authority and a genuinely cheaper flat.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her lead queue while the household rent still needs two wages.
whatWouldHelp: **Written closure dates**, paid human correction and a real job notice with weekly pay and hours would help.
